subject.title: fix(sessions_send): omit misleading delivery.status from async A2A responses (#96020)

question: Should async `sessions_send` A2A responses omit `delivery` metadata, or should OpenClaw expose explicit status values for target-run and announce delivery state?
rationale: Both open candidate PRs fix the stale pending signal but choose different response contracts, and this PR changes metadata that tool consumers may already read.

options.title: Accept omitted async delivery after proof
options.body: Keep this PR's contract shape, require a real OpenClaw `sessions_send` proof run, and land it once maintainers accept the optional-field compatibility impact.

options.title: Choose explicit statuses instead
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers prefer the sibling status-value contract after it becomes proof-positive and semantically precise.

options.title: Keep pending until a larger contract is designed
options.body: Reject both narrow metadata changes for now and track a fuller delivery-status/query contract separately.

recommendation.title: Accept omitted async delivery after proof
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's contract shape, require a real OpenClaw `sessions_send` proof run, and land it once maintainers accept the optional-field compatibility impact.
